name: Hemoglobin Bart's Fetalis Syndrome
aliases: Hydrops fetalis due to Hemoglobin Bart's

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and laboratory diagnosis of Hemoglobin Bart's Fetalis

criteria.description: Absence or near absence of alpha-globin chain production due to deletion of all four alpha-globin genes
Presence of severe fetal hydrops characterized by generalized edema, ascites, and pleural/pericardial effusions
Detection of predominantly Hemoglobin Bart's (γ4) on fetal or neonatal hemoglobin electrophoresis
Prenatal ultrasound showing cardiomegaly, hepatosplenomegaly, and severe anemia
Positive family history of alpha-thalassemia or carrier status in parents

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe alpha-globin gene deletions causing absent alpha-globin production, clinical evidence of hydrops fetalis, and confirmation of Hemoglobin Bart's on electrophoresis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often confirmed prenatally via molecular genetic testing or postnatally by hemoglobin analysis.

laboratory: Hemoglobin electrophoresis showing predominant Hemoglobin Bart's (γ4)
Low or absent alpha-globin chain synthesis
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing hydrops fetalis, cardiomegaly, hepatosplenomegaly, pleural and pericardial effusions
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and effusions
other: Prenatal diagnosis by chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis

distinguishingFeatures: Evidence of hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn
Varied etiologies including cardiac, chromosomal, or metabolic causes

redFlags: Severe fetal hydrops with rapid progression
Marked anemia unresponsive to intrauterine transfusion
references: Orphanet: Hemoglobin Bart's Fetalis Syndrome - ORPHA:163596
